about: The first three exchanges are Psalm 84:7–8 and Psalm 101:2 in the Vulgate numbering, from the Gallican psalter the Mass uses: it opens the first of them Deus, tu convérsus where later editions read Nonne tu convérsus. The last is the liturgical greeting “Dóminus vobíscum” and its response.

seg.tr: O God, You will turn toward us and give us life.

fn.w003: A passive participle used reflexively: “having turned”.

seg.tr: And Your people will rejoice in You.

fn.w009: A future parallel to “vivificábis” (w004): the people will rejoice in God.

seg.tr: Show us Your mercy, O Lord.

fn.w018: Neuter adjective used substantively. Accusative object of “da” (w020).

seg.tr: And let my cry come to You.

fn.w032: Nominal clause without an expressed verb.
fn.w033: The preposition “cum” follows the personal pronoun: “vobís-cum”.

fn.w036: An ablative after “cum” (w035), in the fixed response “Et cum spíritu tuo”.
